transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand the student newspaper has completed an investigative article regarding changes to the school's lunch program, and we're here to go through the pre-publication checklist. Before I record any required changes or make a final decision on the package, I'd like to hear from the journalism adviser and the library media specialist. Could each of you give your brief report on the draft? I'd like to start with understanding the article's sourcing and the materials included — particularly the named student source and the photograph from the school media bank, as well as the plan to publish in both the printed newspaper and on the public school website.

transcript.text: Before I give my full report, I need to flag an important update regarding the student source. After the draft was completed, the student source contacted me and explicitly requested the pseudonym 'River' because the source is a minor concerned about retaliation. I confirmed that the source's statement may be published only with that pseudonym, but I have not yet entered this request in the article file. The current draft still uses the student's real name, so this change needs to be recorded before we proceed.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important issue regarding the photograph from the school media bank. I checked the media-bank license for that photograph this week, and it permits use in the printed newspaper and the school's password-protected internal archive, but it does NOT permit use on the public school website. I should also note that the license record has not yet been attached to the publication request.
